626	### Requirement: Unified Intervention Items
627	
628	All human-in-the-loop interactions inside a running flow MUST be presented as
629	**chips on the docked reply bar**, never as inline cards mixed into the
630	conversation chat-stream. Each chip carries the intervention's kind icon and
631	a short, **user-facing neutral label** describing the interaction kind —
632	implementation-detail vocabulary such as `MCP`, `call_id`, or the
633	literal pattern `call <id>` MUST NOT appear in the chip's visible text. The
634	underlying call identifier, when retained for debugging, lives only on hidden
635	DOM attributes (e.g. `data-call-id`) and `title` hover tooltips, not in any
636	text node a screen reader or sighted user can read. Selecting a chip expands
637	that intervention's `prompt` (Markdown rendered, behind a default-collapsed
638	expand/collapse trigger — see the *Collapsible Reply-Context Prompt Body*
639	requirement) and any `options` action buttons inside the reply context panel
640	above the shared reply textarea; the panel MUST NOT render a separate `context`
641	block for any kind. The same reply textarea is the single input surface for
642	every intervention kind.
643	
644	The recognized intervention kinds are at least: (1) a pending MCP call
645	(`call`); (2) a post-Ctrl-C mid-flow interjection (`interjection`); (3) a
646	retry/failure decision (`retry_decision`); (4) a CLI subprocess confirmation
647	prompt (`cli_confirm`); (5) a non-interactive discovery confirmation gate
648	(`discovery_confirm`). Each chip is derived from a `pending_calls` entry
649	whose `kind` field identifies the interaction; an unrecognized `kind`
650	degrades to a plain `call` chip.
651	
652	A `discovery_confirm` chip is produced when a discovery flow pauses at the
653	programmatic confirmation gate (see the `flow-engine` *Discovery Workflow*
654	requirement) — whether that flow was daemon-spawned (non-interactive) or
655	started interactively from the CLI, because the interactive pause is now
656	mirrored to the same `se3/calls/` call file so the web console can answer it
657	in the live process (terminal and web are awaited in parallel; whichever
658	answers first drives the flow). The chip carries the LLM's refined task
659	description in its `prompt` and at least one `options` entry encoding the
660	one-click confirm action whose **value is the literal `"1"`** — the exact
661	token the gate's `== "1"` check expects. The reply context panel MUST render
662	both affordances side by side: a GUI confirm button (clicking it sends `"1"`
663	through the same call/response reply channel every other chip uses) **and**
664	the `Enter 1 to confirm` textual hint as a fallback, so a user who ignores the button
665	can still type `1`. Because the confirm value is fixed by the gate, the
666	frontend MUST guarantee the confirm button even when the backend call file
667	omitted the `options` array — it synthesizes a single confirm option whose
668	value is `"1"` so the button and the textual hint always coexist.
669	
670	The reply context panel MUST NOT render a separate `context` block for **any**
671	intervention kind. The `context` text duplicates information the `prompt`
672	already carries (e.g. a `discovery_confirm` whose `prompt` embeds the refined
673	task description and whose backend also mirrors it into
674	`context.refined_description`), so rendering it would repeat the same content
675	directly below the prompt. This context suppression is **uniform across all
676	kinds** (`call` / `interjection` / `retry_decision` / `cli_confirm` /
677	`discovery_confirm`); `discovery_confirm` is no longer a special case — every
678	kind renders only the kind header, the Markdown prompt, and any `options`
679	buttons.
680	
681	A synthetic `interjection` chip is **opt-in**, not always-on: an active flow
682	that is not already waiting on a real interjection MUST render an inline
683	Interject icon button at the left end of the reply input row (symmetric to
684	Send); clicking the button materializes a synthetic `interjection` chip and
685	selects it. The reply textarea itself stays enabled at all times so the user
686	can draft text freely — only the Send button is gated, and it is enabled
687	when (a) the user has opted into interjection or (b) a real pending
688	call/interjection is waiting. A successful interjection send consumes the
689	opt-in (the synthetic chip disappears and the inline Interject button
690	returns to its inactive state until the user clicks it again).
691	
692	Expanding a folded long record or showing a raw-payload toggle MUST keep the
693	newly-revealed content visible: after the expand transition the consumer
694	SHOULD call `Element.scrollIntoView({block: "nearest"})` on the freshly
695	shown block so content past the viewport edge scrolls into view. Collapse
696	does **not** scroll — collapsing should leave the reader's current position
697	untouched.
698	
699	#### Scenario: Each intervention kind is rendered as a chip on the reply bar
700	- **WHEN** a running flow has a pending interaction of kind `call`,
701	  `interjection`, `retry_decision`, or `cli_confirm`
702	- **THEN** it is rendered as a status-style chip button in the docked reply
703	  chip bar
704	- **AND** the chip is not rendered as a message card inside the chat-stream
705	
706	#### Scenario: Discovery confirmation chip offers a confirm button and a textual fallback
707	- **GIVEN** a daemon-spawned discovery flow has paused at the programmatic
708	  confirmation gate, surfacing a `pending_calls` entry of kind
709	  `discovery_confirm` whose `prompt` carries the refined task description
710	- **WHEN** the user selects the chip
711	- **THEN** the reply context panel renders a GUI confirm button whose click
712	  sends the literal `"1"` through the shared call/response reply channel
713	- **AND** the panel also shows the `Enter 1 to confirm` textual hint so the user can
714	  type `1` manually instead
715	- **AND** when the backend call file omitted the `options` array, the frontend
716	  still synthesizes the confirm button with value `"1"`
717	
718	#### Scenario: Discovery confirmation chip does not duplicate the refined description
719	- **GIVEN** a `discovery_confirm` chip whose `prompt` already contains the
720	  refined task description and whose `context.refined_description` carries the
721	  same text
722	- **WHEN** the user selects the chip
723	- **THEN** the reply context panel renders the prompt and the confirm
724	  affordances but does NOT render the `context` block beneath the prompt
725	- **AND** every other intervention kind (`call` / `interjection` /
726	  `retry_decision` / `cli_confirm`) likewise renders no `context` block — the
727	  context suppression is uniform across all kinds, not a `discovery_confirm`
728	  special case
729	
730	#### Scenario: Selecting a chip expands its prompt and options above the textarea
731	- **WHEN** the user selects an intervention chip
732	- **THEN** the reply context panel above the textarea shows the
733	  intervention's kind header, its Markdown-rendered `prompt` behind a
734	  default-collapsed expand/collapse trigger (see *Collapsible Reply-Context
735	  Prompt Body*), and any `options` action buttons — and renders no separate
736	  `context` block
737	- **AND** the reply textarea + send button are enabled
738	- **AND** the same textarea is reused as the reply input regardless of
739	  intervention kind
740	
741	#### Scenario: Unknown kind degrades to a plain call chip
742	- **WHEN** a `pending_calls` entry carries a `kind` value that is not one of
743	  the recognized kinds
744	- **THEN** it is rendered as a plain `call` chip
745	
746	#### Scenario: Reply box targets a single intervention
747	- **WHEN** multiple intervention chips are present in the chip bar
748	- **THEN** at most one chip is selected at any time
749	- **AND** the reply context panel + reply textarea target exactly the
750	  selected intervention
751	
752	#### Scenario: No implementation vocabulary in visible chip text
753	- **GIVEN** the chip bar renders chips for every recognized intervention
754	  kind (`call`, `interjection`, `retry_decision`, `cli_confirm`)
755	- **WHEN** the rendered chip DOM is inspected
756	- **THEN** the visible text content of every chip MUST NOT contain the
757	  substrings `MCP`, `call_id`, or the pattern `call <hex-id>`
758	- **AND** any preserved call identifier appears only on the chip's
759	  `data-call-id` attribute or `title` tooltip, never in visible text

761	### Requirement: Collapsible Reply-Context Prompt Body
762	
763	The docked reply context panel (`updateReplyBox` in `app.js`) MUST NOT render a
764	selected intervention's `prompt` as an unbounded, always-expanded block. A long
765	`prompt` — most notably a `discovery_confirm` whose `prompt` embeds an entire
766	refined task description — would otherwise grow the `.flow-reply-prompt` body
767	without limit and push the height-bounded reply controls (kind header, any
768	synthesized confirm / `options` buttons, the reply textarea, and the Send
769	button) out of the viewport, leaving them unreachable. To prevent this, the
770	prompt body MUST be mounted as a **default-collapsed, expand-on-demand block**
771	with a **height-bounded, internally scrollable** expanded state. This scope is
772	strictly limited to `#flow-view`'s reply-context panel (the sole consumer of the
773	collapsible-prompt helper); the history view and all other surfaces are
774	untouched.
775	
776	The structure is built by a pure helper (`buildCollapsiblePrompt`, exported for
777	DOM-stub tests) and has these properties:
778	
779	1. **Default collapsed** — when a chip is first selected, the `.flow-reply-prompt`
780	   Markdown body is rendered but hidden by default (e.g. a `.hidden` class
781	   mapping to `display: none`), so the panel's initial height carries only the
782	   kind header, the expand/collapse trigger, the `options` / confirm buttons, the
783	   textarea, and Send. This loses no information: the prompt body is redundant
784	   with the conversation chat-stream for every kind (a `call` prompt is the agent
785	   turn text; `cli_confirm` enters the stream via `StreamJSONTracker`;
786	   `retry_decision` surfaces as a `step_failed` card; the `discovery_confirm`
787	   refined description already appears as an assistant message; `interjection`
788	   carries no prompt).
789	2. **Expand/collapse trigger** — an always-visible toggle control (e.g.
790	   "▸ expand message details" / "▾ collapse") sits above the body; clicking it
791	   toggles the body's visibility. Expanding calls
792	   `Element.scrollIntoView({block: "nearest"})` (via `requestAnimationFrame`) on
793	   the freshly shown body so the revealed content scrolls into view; collapsing
794	   does NOT scroll, consistent with the view's other foldable affordances.
795	3. **Height-bounded expanded body** — when expanded, the `.flow-reply-prompt`
796	   body MUST be capped at a viewport-relative maximum height (currently
797	   `max-height: 30vh`) with `overflow-y: auto`, so a prompt of any length
798	   occupies at most that fixed fraction of the viewport and is scrolled
799	   internally. The body MUST also keep horizontal overflow out (`overflow-x:
800	   hidden`) and wrap long lines (`overflow-wrap: anywhere` / `word-break`), per
801	   the *Long-Content Wrapping* requirement. The kind header, expand trigger,
802	   `options` / confirm buttons, textarea, and Send button all sit OUTSIDE this
803	   height-capped region and therefore remain visible and clickable regardless of
804	   prompt length.
805	
806	The expand state is persisted as a session-level UI preference keyed by
807	intervention id (e.g. `call:<callId>`), so a user's manual expand/collapse
808	choice survives automatic re-renders (STATUS_UPDATE / ws push →
809	renderInterventions → updateReplyBox). The persisted map is reset when
810	opening or closing `#flow-view`, so switching to a different flow or
811	closing the view returns to the default collapsed state. The synthesized
812	`discovery_confirm` confirm button (see *Unified Intervention Items*) and all
813	other `options` buttons remain outside the collapsible body so they are reachable
814	without expanding the prompt.
815	
816	#### Scenario: Long prompt is collapsed by default and never pushes controls off-screen
817	- **GIVEN** a selected intervention chip (e.g. `discovery_confirm`) whose
818	  `prompt` is very long (an embedded refined task description)
819	- **WHEN** the reply context panel is rendered
820	- **THEN** the `.flow-reply-prompt` Markdown body is hidden by default behind an
821	  expand/collapse trigger
822	- **AND** the panel's kind header, any confirm / `options` buttons, the reply
823	  textarea, and the Send button are all visible and clickable without expanding
824	  the prompt
825	
826	#### Scenario: Expanding the prompt bounds its height and scrolls internally
827	- **GIVEN** a selected chip whose prompt body is collapsed
828	- **WHEN** the user clicks the expand trigger
829	- **THEN** the `.flow-reply-prompt` body becomes visible, capped at the
830	  configured maximum height (`max-height: 30vh`) with `overflow-y: auto`, so an
831	  arbitrarily long prompt scrolls inside that fixed region rather than growing
832	  the panel
833	- **AND** the body is scrolled into view via
834	  `scrollIntoView({block: "nearest"})` on expand
835	- **AND** the header, trigger, `options` buttons, textarea, and Send button
836	  remain outside the height-capped region and stay visible
837	
838	#### Scenario: Collapsing the prompt does not scroll, and expand state persists across re-render
839	- **GIVEN** an expanded prompt body
840	- **WHEN** the user clicks the trigger to collapse it
841	- **THEN** the body is hidden again and the view does NOT scroll
842	- **AND** the collapsed state is persisted so that subsequent automatic
843	  re-renders (e.g. a new snapshot) keep the prompt collapsed
844	- **AND** when `#flow-view` is closed or a different flow is opened, the
845	  expand state resets to the default collapsed

847	### Requirement: Interjection Lifecycle Events
848	
849	A web-console interjection's full lifecycle — **pending** (call file just
850	written by the daemon, not yet drained by the run loop) and **consumed**
851	(drained by the run loop, the call file gone) — MUST be observable to the
852	frontend through the `/ws/ui` channel, so the operator gets visible
853	feedback for every interjection they send instead of a silent "did it
854	work?" gap.
855	
856	The lifecycle is carried as a lightweight UI-side event, `interjection_event`,
857	broadcast by the server's `/ws/ui` channel and derived from the daemon's
858	`STATUS_UPDATE` `pending_calls` diff (no new daemon↔server protocol message
859	type is added — see `base` spec's *Daemon Modules* / *Server Modules*
860	requirements). Each event carries at least `flow_id`, `call_id`, and a
861	`phase` field whose value is one of `pending` or `consumed`. The diff
862	detection happens in `ws.py` (the `STATUS_UPDATE` handling path), so an
863	upstream daemon that has not been upgraded still produces consistent
864	events as long as it reports current `pending_calls`.
865	
866	To make the diff itself responsive — instead of waiting for the daemon's
867	~5-second `status_interval` tick — the daemon's interjection write path
868	and consumption-detection path MUST trigger an out-of-band immediate
869	status push (`_fast_push_event` in `DaemonClient` or equivalent) so the
870	lifecycle event reaches `/ws/ui` within ~1 second of either the call file
871	appearing or its sibling `.response` being written / the call file being
872	unlinked.
873	
874	The frontend MUST deduplicate `interjection_event`s per
875	`(call_id, phase)` to ensure each lifecycle transition triggers exactly
876	one toast / chip state change. The chip's visible state and the toast
877	text MUST track the real lifecycle: a freshly written interjection
878	appears as a `pending` chip with a "waiting for the flow to drain"
879	phrasing; a `consumed` event flips the chip into a consumed visual state
880	(or removes it, matched against the history-jsonl interjection record
881	that the run loop now also writes) and updates the toast accordingly.
882	The toast MUST NOT claim the interjection "took effect" earlier than the
883	`consumed` event arrives.
884	
885	#### Scenario: Pending event surfaces on the chip bar
886	- **GIVEN** the user submits an interjection through the docked reply box
887	  for a running flow
888	- **WHEN** the daemon writes the `interjection`-kind call file under that
889	  flow's `se3/calls/` and triggers an immediate status push
890	- **THEN** the `/ws/ui` channel broadcasts an `interjection_event` whose
891	  `phase` is `pending` and whose `flow_id` / `call_id` identify the call
892	- **AND** the frontend shows the pending interjection in the chip bar and
893	  surfaces a toast acknowledging that the interjection is queued
894	
895	#### Scenario: Consumed event reflects run-loop drain
896	- **GIVEN** a `pending` interjection event for `(flow_id, call_id)` is
897	  already on screen
898	- **WHEN** the run loop drains the call file (writing the sibling
899	  `.response` then unlinking) and the daemon fast-pushes the resulting
900	  `pending_calls` diff
901	- **THEN** the `/ws/ui` channel broadcasts a second `interjection_event`
902	  for the same `(flow_id, call_id)` with `phase = consumed`
903	- **AND** the frontend transitions the chip to a consumed state (or
904	  removes it) and updates the toast to reflect that the interjection was
905	  taken in by the flow
906	
907	#### Scenario: Frontend dedupes events by (call_id, phase)
908	- **WHEN** the daemon emits two `STATUS_UPDATE`s in quick succession that
909	  both diff to the same `interjection_event` for `(call_id, phase)`
910	- **THEN** the frontend MUST apply exactly one chip / toast transition
911	  for that `(call_id, phase)` pair, not one per `STATUS_UPDATE`
912	- **AND** the dedup MUST NOT swallow the **next** phase event for the
913	  same `call_id` (e.g. a later `consumed` after a `pending`)
914	
915	### Requirement: Conversation Strict Chronological Order
916	
917	All records that ride a running flow's conversation channel — `user`,
918	`assistant`, `system`, the `step_completed` / `step_failed` events surfaced
919	as report cards, and any other in-stream record — MUST be rendered in a
920	**single strict chronological order keyed by record timestamp**, across all
921	roles AND across all step boundaries. Step grouping is allowed only as a
922	*visual* affordance (e.g. a lightweight `.history-step-header` separator row
923	inserted between adjacent records whose step changes); it MUST NOT shuffle
924	records out of timestamp order. Concretely: a `user` reply produced between
925	two `assistant` outputs of a `discovery` step MUST appear between them in
926	the rendered timeline, even if the `user` reply's `step_id` momentarily
927	classifies it under a different step section.
928	
929	The ordering key is `(timestamp, original-index)`: records with equal
930	timestamps preserve the input order they arrived in (stable sort by NDJSON
931	position). Records that arrive late (e.g. via incremental append) MUST be
932	inserted into their correct global slot, not unconditionally appended at the

3	:class:`DaemonHistoryReader` enumerates the ``se3 history`` artifacts of every
4	project root the daemon tracks and turns them into:
5	
6	* a *session index* — one :class:`SessionMeta` per known flow (flow id, task
7	  description, status, timestamps, active flag) — reported to the central
8	  server via :data:`~se3.daemon.protocol.MSG_HISTORY_INDEX` so the web UI can

27	Cursor model

These all look correct - they clear progress when switching flows or closing the view. Now, let me think through the two bugs:

## Bug 1: After pressing "1" to confirm, subsequent messages don't appear

The user presses Send → `sendReply` succeeds → `appendLocalReply` adds echo to state → receives success toast → but then NO new messages appear in the ws `history_data` stream.

This could happen if:
1. The respond endpoint doesn't properly forward the project_root
2. The daemon receives the respond but doesn't push history updates
3. The ws connection breaks and doesn't reconnect
4. The server suppresses the history_data broadcast (see line 1091-1100 in ws.py)

Looking at lines 1087-1100 in ws.py again - the server SUPPRESSES the UI broadcast of `history_data` when it resolved a pull waiter. This is intentional - the REST handler reads the cache and returns to clients directly. But the comment says "Live active-flow appends never resolve a waiter, so they still stream normally."

So the issue might be: **after the respond succeeds, the daemon sends a `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` with mode="append" that resolves a pending pull, which SUPPRESSES the ws broadcast, but then the ui client has no way to be notified of new messages since the REST pull already resolved and the ws broadcast was suppressed.**

## Bug 2: Worktree session - no messages appear, even the first reply doesn't show content

The spec mentions at line 1386: "no message after the first renders as "(no readable content)"". This suggests the worktree session's history files are not being merged correctly.

Looking at the history.py code, the `_iter_history_jsonl` function should include sidecar files. But maybe the issue is on the **daemon send side** - maybe when the daemon pushes history_data for a worktree session, it's not including all the records?

Let me create a comprehensive summary now:

Based on my investigation, here are my findings:

## Frontend Code (History & Streaming)

**File: `/data/cre/workspace/se3.0/se3/worktrees/worktree-webui-1-session-bug-bug-20260614-150938-2d556aa7/src/se3/server/static/app.js**

### Key Functions:

1. **`sendReply(flowId, target, text)` — lines 2390-2496**
   - User submits reply via Send button
   - Posts to `/api/flows/{flowId}/respond` or `/api/flows/{flowId}/interject`
   - On `resp.ok`: clears input, shows success toast, calls `appendLocalReply` for optimistic echo
   - On error: shows "Could not send" error toast

2. **`appendLocalReply(flowId, target, text)` — lines 2506-2577**
   - Appends optimistic echo record to `state.flowConversationRecords` (state-first, before rendering)
   - Renders conversation with best-effort try/catch around rendering helpers
   - Helps with instant feedback for user

3. **`applyHistoryData(msg)` — lines 2656-2716**
   - Receives websocket `history_data` push from server
   - **Running-flow branch (lines 2689-2715)**: if append mode, dedups against existing records via `dedupeAppendRecords`, merges fresh records, reconciles local echoes, renders
   - If mode="full", replaces entire records array and clears progress token
   - Calls `dedupeAppendRecords` to prevent duplicate rendering when same batch hits REST snapshot and WS append

4. **`loadFlowConversation(flowId, opts)` — lines 1538-1629**
   - Loads or refreshes flow conversation from `/api/history/{flowId}` 
   - First-open sends no `after` token (gets full snapshot)
   - Reconnect sends held `flowConversationProgress` token via `?after=` query param (gets delta or full fallback)
   - Merges via `mergeHistoryResponse`, reconciles local echoes, renders

5. **`mergeHistoryResponse(response, existing, requestBaseline)` — lines 4444-4526**
   - On `delivery: "delta"`: appends fresh deduplicated records
   - On `delivery: "full"`: replaces bundle and preserves pending local echoes
   - Returns `{ records, progress, render }` tuple

## Backend Code (Server History Relay)

**File: `/data/cre/workspace/se3.0/se3/worktrees/worktree-webui-1-session-bug-bug-20260614-150938-2d556aa7/src/se3/server/app.py**

### Key Endpoints:

1. **`POST /api/flows/{flow_id}/respond` — lines 617-652**
   - Gets flow via `state.get_flow(flow_id, owner=...)`
   - Calls `protocol.make_respond_call(call_id, response, project_root=flow.get("project_root", ""))`
   - Sends message to daemon via `manager.send_to(machine_id, message)`

2. **`POST /api/flows/{flow_id}/interject` — lines 655-689**
   - Similar flow to respond
   - Calls `protocol.make_interject_flow(flow_id, text, project_root=flow.get("project_root", ""))`

3. **`GET /api/history/{flow_id}` — lines 1549-1664**
   - Cache hit: returns full or delta snapshot atomically
   - Cache miss: dispatches `MSG_HISTORY_REQUEST` to daemon, waits for reply
   - Holds `HistoryRequestRegistry` to deduplicate concurrent requests for same flow

**File: `/data/cre/workspace/se3.0/se3/worktrees/worktree-webui-1-session-bug-bug-20260614-150938-2d556aa7/src/se3/server/ws.py**

### Key Functions:

1. **`MSG_HISTORY_DATA` handler — lines 1055-1100**
   - Daemon sends history records with `mode` (append/full) and optional `cursor`
   - Calls `state.append_history(flow_id, mode, records, cursor, machine_id=machine_id)` to cache
   - **CRITICAL**: If cached and a pull waiter was pending (rest handler blocked), resolves it
   - **CRITICAL**: Only broadcasts to UI (`_push_history_data`) if **NOT** resolving a pull waiter
   - Comment says: "re-broadcasting the same `mode: full` frame over `/ws/ui` would make every history consumer reset its progress to null… Live active-flow appends never resolve a waiter, so they still stream normally."

2. **`_push_history_data(hub, state, machine_id, flow_id, mode, records)` — lines 716-736**
   - Broadcasts `{"type": "history_data", "flow_id": flow_id, "mode": mode, "records": records}` to UI clients
   - Scoped to machine owner

**File: `/data/cre/workspace/se3.0/se3/worktrees/worktree-webui-1-session-bug-bug-20260614-150938-2d556aa7/src/se3/server/state.py**

### Key Methods:

1. **`append_history(flow_id, mode, records, cursor, machine_id)` — lines 599-687**
   - Caches history records in-memory at `self._history_data[flow_id]`
   - On append mode with no existing cache: marks `_history_requires_full[flow_id]` and returns False
   - On append mode with `_history_requires_full` flag set: discards the append and returns False
   - On append mode with existing cache: extends records and returns True
   - On full/other mode: replaces bundle, clears the `_history_requires_full` flag, returns True

## Daemon Code (History Push)

**File: `/data/cre/workspace/se3.0/se3/worktrees/worktree-webui-1-session-bug-bug-20260614-150938-2d556aa7/src/se3/daemon/history.py**

### Key Functions:

1. **`read_flow(flow_id, project_root, cursor)` — lines 617-830**
   - Reads per-step history files incrementally using line cursors
   - Iterates via `_iter_history_jsonl(flow_dir)` which includes both primary `*.jsonl` AND sidecar `*.jsonl.from-*` files
   - Merges sidecars under same logical step_id via `_logical_step_id(filename)`
   - Returns `FlowRead(mode, records, cursor)` with cursor mapping filename to line count

2. **`_iter_history_jsonl(flow_dir)` — lines 1002-1021**
   - **IMPORTANT**: Includes both `glob("*.jsonl")` and `glob("*.jsonl.from-*")` files
   - Comment says: "The plain `glob("*.jsonl")` never matched the sidecars, so a worktree session's conversation after its first record was silently dropped — this helper restores it."

3. **`_logical_step_id(filename)` — lines 982-999**
   - Strips `.jsonl` extension AND any `.from-<branch>` suffix
   - Collapses primary and sidecar files to same step id

## Hypotheses for the Two Bugs

### Bug 1: Subsequent messages don't appear after pressing "1" to confirm

**Root Cause Hypothesis:**
The issue is likely in the **ws.py daemon-message handler** at lines 1087-1100. When the user sends a respond and the daemon's first history_data push arrives:

1. The respond succeeds (user sees toast "Response sent")
2. `appendLocalReply` adds the optimistic echo to state
3. The daemon writes a history record and sends `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` with the new record
4. The server's `ws.py` handler receives it, calls `state.append_history()` which returns `True` (cache updated)
5. **BUT** if there's a pending REST pull waiter (from `loadFlowConversation` re-fetching), the handler **resolves that waiter** and **suppresses the ws broadcast**
6. The ui client waiting on the ws `history_data` append never receives the update
7. The REST waiter gets served the cached data, but the ui client never subscribed to that REST response
8. **Result**: UI has local echo in state but ws never pushes the authoritative record, so subsequent updates never appear

**Evidence**: Comments in ws.py lines 1087-1100 and app.js lines 2656-2715 show the dedup logic assumes either a ws push OR a REST response will deliver the records, but there's a race where the ws broadcast is suppressed while the REST handler re-fetches independently.

### Bug 2: `--worktree` session shows no messages after first record

**Root Cause Hypothesis:**
This is likely a **state management issue on the daemon side** when handling worktree flows. The fix to include sidecar files in `_iter_history_jsonl` is in place, but:

1. The daemon reads history correctly from both primary and sidecar files
2. BUT when the daemon **sends** `MSG_HISTORY_DATA`, it may be using stale cursor state or wrong file enumeration
3. OR the cursor-tracking in `read_flow` doesn't properly handle sidecar files advancing the line count
4. **OR** the project_root in the respond message is used to look up the flow in the wrong directory for worktree sessions

The spec at line 1386 says "no message after the first renders as "(no readable content)"" which suggests the records ARE being fetched but their content is corrupted or normalized incorrectly for worktree sessions.

**Evidence**: The history.py code shows `_iter_history_jsonl` was fixed to include sidecars (line 1010-1011), but this fix may not be consistently applied to all code paths, or the worktree flow's project_root may not be correctly preserved through the respond/interject endpoints.

---

## Files to Investigate Further

1. **`src/se3/server/static/app.js`**: lines 1538-1629 (loadFlowConversation), 2656-2716 (applyHistoryData), 4444-4526 (mergeHistoryResponse)
2. **`src/se3/server/ws.py`**: lines 1055-1100 (history_data handler), 716-736 (_push_history_data)
3. **`src/se3/server/state.py`**: lines 599-687 (append_history)
4. **`src/se3/daemon/history.py`**: lines 617-830 (read_flow), 1002-1021 (_iter_history_jsonl), 982-999 (_logical_step_id)

### Bug 1: Subsequent messages don't appear after pressing "1" to confirm

**Root Cause Hypothesis:**
The issue is likely in the **ws.py daemon-message handler** at lines 1087-1100. When the user sends a respond and the daemon's first history_data push arrives:

1. The respond succeeds (user sees toast "Response sent")
2. `appendLocalReply` adds the optimistic echo to state
3. The daemon writes a history record and sends `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` with the new record

7. The REST waiter gets served the cached data, but the ui client never subscribed to that REST response
8. **Result**: UI has local echo in state but ws never pushes the authoritative record, so subsequent updates never appear
